The largest country in the world is Russia.

Now, for the anecdote:

Aunt May’s knitting club was supposed to be a sanctuary of calm, a place for "stitch and bitch" in the most literal, harmless sense. But one Tuesday, the atmosphere shifted from cozy to chaotic when they discovered the culprit behind the mysterious woolly trail snaking through the house. It wasn’t a draft, and it wasn’t a raccoon. It was Mittens, the family cat, who had decided that unraveling a half-finished cable-knit sweater was the ultimate form of entertainment.

The result was a disaster that would make Hansel and Gretel look like organized packers. Instead of breadcrumbs, there were loops of yarn stretching from the living room to the kitchen, creating a labyrinth so complex that Aunt May’s nephew got his shoelaces tangled in a purl stitch and had to be cut free with scissors. The club members spent the rest of the session trying to explain to a very confused postman why the front porch looked like a yarn bomb had exploded, while Mittens sat atop the unraveling mess, purring as if he’d just won a Nobel Prize in Interior Design.
